The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) celebrates three significant achievements after receiving three favorable audit reports from the Commission on Audit (COA) across three areas, a testament to the agency’s unwavering commitment to good governance and effective public service delivery.

The audit reports came before the order of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to audit all flood control projects during yesterday's State of the Nation Address (SONA).

MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes said the first notable report is the COA’s Citizen Participatory Audit on the flood control projects of the MMDA; second, unmodified opinion for the agency’s financial reporting for six consecutive years; and favorable audit report for Metro Manila Flood Management Project (MMFMP) Phase-1.

“These COA reports affirm and validate the agency’s efforts to reduce flooding in Metro Manila, aligned with the President’s directive under the Bagong Pilipinas vision to reinforce and optimize flood control systems in vulnerable areas,” said Artes.

‘A significant decrease in flooding’ was noted in the Citizen Participatory Audit (CPA) for select flood control projects of MMDA from January 1, 2021 to June 30, 2024, where those directly affected and serviced by the selected projects and implemented in the said period said they are satisfied with the projects and interventions undertaken by the agency.

State auditors found that the agency ensured availability of appropriations and/or allotments prior to the procurement and implementation of flood control projects. Audit findings also include MMDA being compliant with disbursement transactions for the selected completed flood control projects.

Meanwhile, data from the survey revealed that flood severity and frequency have declined in recent years. Audit results said reports of waist to chest-deep floodings dropped from 43% before 2020 to 23% after 2021.

Those experiencing minor or no flooding slightly rose from 31% to 39%. Sharp decline on disruptions caused by flooding was also noted from 55% to 26%. Moreover, frequent flooding has likewise decreased with 65% reporting nowadays that it happens rarely, occasionally, or not at all.

While there are still lingering concerns on waste disposal, poor drainage system, climate change, and informal settlements, public satisfaction with the flood mitigation efforts stands at 82%.

Noting the significant improvements on flood mitigation efforts made by the agency, Artes said that the agency is conducting regular maintenance works in ensuring that all its flood mitigation projects are operational, heeding the directive of the President.

“The MMDA recognizes the significance of ensuring that its flood control and mitigation projects are at full operating capacity. Year-round conduct of inspection and maintenance of 71 pumping stations as well as drainage improvement on various locations in Metro Manila are religiously done to ensure full capacity and effectiveness,” he said.

The MMDA chief also reiterated his appeal to the public to be responsible and disciplined in managing their solid waste as this is integral in addressing the flood problems in NCR.

Minor audit findings were being addressed already by the agency such as formulation of strategies to address manpower issues, among others.

CPA is a technique in conducting audits with citizens as members of COA Audit Teams aimed to promote transparency and encourage active citizen involvement in the audit process.

The audit team was composed of COA Central Office Technical Inspection Team, NGOs, & civil society groups. Respondents of the survey were residents serviced by various pumping stations & flood control projects in the metro.

UNMODIFIED OPINION FROM COA FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024
The MMDA has received another unmodified opinion from the Commission on Audit (COA) for its financial reporting for fiscal year (FY) 2024 — continuing its six-year streak.
The unmodified opinion, or an unqualified opinion, is issued when the auditor concludes that the financial statements are prepared in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.
Artes expressed his utmost gratitude to COA for awarding the agency the highest audit rating for FY 2024.
“We at MMDA are grateful to the COA for its impartial evaluation of our financial reporting and auditing standards. This proves that the agency’s financial statements reported were accurately prepared and validates our unwavering commitment to good governance," Artes said.
The Independent Auditor’s Report, transmitted by the COA to MMDA, stated, "In our opinion, the accompanying financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the MMDA as of December 31, 2024, and its financial performance, changes in net assets/equity, cash flows, and the comparison of budget and actual amounts for the year then ended in accordance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSASs)."
The report further noted: “We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion.”
According to the COA, it conducted its audit in accordance with International Standards of Supreme Audit Institutions (ISSAIs), the authoritative international standards on public sector auditing.
MMFMP PHASE 1 EARNS FAVORABLE AUDIT REPORT
Meanwhile, the Metro Manila Flood Management Project (MMFMP) Phase 1 received a favorable audit report for fair presentation of financial statements for fiscal year 2024.
“The COA report for MMFMP Phase 1's financial statements underscores the agency's commitment to transparency and accountability in managing public funds, ensuring they are utilized effectively and responsibly. This milestone is an indication that the project is on solid financial footing and progressing efficiently towards its goal of reducing flood risk in flood prone areas in Metro Manila and improving solid waste management near select waterways,” said Artes.
The COA transmitted to MMDA a copy of the Independent Auditor's Report penned by Supervising Auditor Atty. Tracy Ann Sunico, citing that “the accompanying financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the MMFMP Phase 1 as of December 31, 2024, and its financial performance, changes in net assets/equity, cash flows, and the comparison of budget and actual amounts for the year then ended in accordance with IPSASs.”
The MMDA is in-charge of the implementation of the MMFMP’s Component 2 (Minimizing Solid Waste in Waterways) which aims to improve solid waste management in barangays surrounding the pumping stations that will ultimately help maintain their efficiency.
MMFMP's community engagement and innovative solutions is paving the way for a cleaner and greener environment in Metro Manila. #mmda
